paragraphs: Eliphaz says some beautiful things about God. He calls Him the One who does "great and unsearchable things" (Job 5:9), and says "He wounds, but He also binds" (Job 5:18). Friend, frame those lines and hang them on a wall, they'd look GREAT. The trouble is what Eliphaz does with them next.

He asks, "Who, being innocent, has ever perished?" (Job 4:7), and I think he's hinting that Job's pain points back to Job. But the story already told us Job was "blameless and upright" (Job 1:1). Friend, that's like showing up to comfort somebody with a clipboard instead of a hug. A true thing about God, bent into the wrong answer for the person in front of you, is a LOT of clipboard and not much comfort.

So here's the big idea, baker: weigh every word about God and suffering against all of Scripture, even when it sounds wise and comes from a friend. Eliphaz does get one thing right when he says he would "appeal to God" (Job 5:8). Bring your hurt to God, and when someone else is hurting, bring them comfort before you bring them a theory. Job's story is a LONG way from over, and there's much more to hear.
